D013-D009_h001.question: Lately, it feels like I'm moving through mud, even with my favorite elephants. Getting out of bed is a monumental effort, and I drag myself around the enclosures, feeling sluggish and heavy. Everything seems to take an eternity. I’ve been crying a lot too, often for no reason at all, just sudden bursts of tears I can’t stop, and my wife looks at me with such concern. All I can think about are the mistakes I’ve made, little things from years ago, blowing them up in my head until I feel like a complete failure. There are moments when I'm walking near the lion exhibit, and this terrifying urge springs up – to just jump in, or if I’m driving, to swerve into oncoming traffic, even though I don't really want to die. It's been like this for about five months now, making it almost impossible to focus on my duties. Sometimes I get brief bursts of energy, feeling pretty good for an hour or so, a slight lift in my mood, but it never lasts, and it's certainly never enough to make me feel like I’m truly on top of the world or doing crazy things, and I've assured my doctor I've never experienced such an episode before.

A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Adjustment Disorder

D013-D009_h002.question:
It's been about five months now that I’ve felt this dark cloud hanging over me. I just can’t seem to get over this overwhelming sadness; some days I find myself just openly weeping for no apparent reason, which isn’t like me at all. My mind’s always racing, I can't sit still for a second – picking at my cuticles, pacing my apartment late into the night. And the guilt… it's crushing. I feel personally responsible for everything that goes wrong, even trivial stuff at work, like a bug in an app update. I keep thinking, "What if I just didn't wake up tomorrow? It would be easier."

Sometimes I get these bursts of energy, like for a day or two I'll feel great, hyper-focused on a new coding project, barely sleeping. I know it sounds a bit like, you know, a hypomanic episode, and I’ve even thought about it, but it never lasts long enough for anyone else to really notice, and definitely not like it did for my friend who got diagnosed bipolar. I've never had a full-blown episode where I was completely out of control, or anything that anyone would call "mania." I just feel on edge and then it crashes back down to this deep despair. It’s definitely getting in the way of my job; I can barely focus on developing my apps anymore.
D013-D009_h002.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Adjustment Disorder
